Implementation Notes & Best Practices: Do's:
Place bulk of message in the top 400px portion of the screen (i.e. above the fold). Include a link or clickable area (i.e. call-to-action) above the fold for optimal click-throughresults.

Include both images and text in creative, rather thanone large image with text embedded within graphic. (If the design requires the creative to be all images, add all text components of the creative to their respective alt tags).
Hardcode all accents (i.e. French) and punctuations (i.e. bullets, ampersands, hyphens).
Host all images, and hardcode the image URL in the HTML code.
Define all cell widths, align, and valign properties.
Define all table widths, borders, cellpadding ,and cellspacing properties.
Insert click tags or tracked URLs in the final HTMLfile.
Avoid URL re-directs or links with .aspx extensions.
Don'ts:
Do not use FLASH, JavaScript, CSS, or DIV tags, as most email clients strip these codes out and render inaccurate displays.
If using CSS, they should be coded in-line, and not in the head tag.
Do not rely on background images (most email clients do not support backgroundimages)
Keep email background white or use an HTML bgcolor as a fallback option.

Note: We apply tracking to all links provided in an eBlast. If you provide an already-tracked link, our email software may run into problems re-tracking that link. Please inform us in advance if your eBlast has tracking.
Advertiser Contact Info: Advertiser’s legal name and mailing address. Plus either a URL or email address or phone number.
Note: Per CASL regulations, the email cannot be deployed without this information.
Test List + Seed Lists: Email addresses for everyone that should receive a test and/or actual email (seed) when deployed.
Quality Assurance: Client/Agency is responsible for QA of the creative before final HTML is submitted.
